beats.text: Part d. The heat absorbed by the calorimeter is the calibration factor times the corrected rise: six hundred times four point eight, which is two thousand eight hundred and eighty joules, or two point eight eight zero kilojoules.

Divide by the amount of the limiting reactant, which equals the amount of water formed: two point eight eight zero kilojoules divided by zero point zero five zero zero moles is fifty-seven point six. The reaction released heat into the calorimeter, so delta H is negative: negative fifty-seven point six, or about negative fifty-eight kilojoules per mole of water. Two significant figures, because the corrected rise has only two.
Three marks: the heat, the division by the limiting amount, and delta H with the correct sign and units.
